extracted.intended_audience: researchers and authors submitting to Royal Society journals (e.g., Royal Society Open Science, Open Biology, Proceedings A/B); journal editors and reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Publisher-level guidance describing Royal Society Publishing's open science policies and requirements for submitting, reviewing, and publishing research (open data, open code, peer review models, registered reports, replications, metrics and citations). Intended to guide authors, reviewers and editors on expectations and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open science features
rubrics_metrics.description: Features of open science include but are not limited to open access, open data, open protocols, open code and transparent peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Royal Society Publishing supports these open science practices across its journals; the page lists these as the core elements the publisher seeks to further in research and publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Royal Society Publishing promotes open access as part of its open science initiatives (top-level statement; specific OA policies are found on journal pages).

rubrics_metrics.name: Open data (condition of publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a condition of publication that authors make available the data, code and research materials supporting the results in the article with an open license (CC0 or CC-BY).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More information is available in the publisher's open data policy, which can be cited by DOI via FAIRsharing.org. The aim is to allow others to verify and build on published work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material licence and deposition
rubrics_metrics.description: All supplementary material (including video) is published under a CC-BY licence alongside the paper on the journal website and deposited on Figshare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content on this dedicated channel (Figshare) is fully searchable and citable. This ensures discoverability and re-use under CC-BY terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article and journal metrics (DORA compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Royal Society Publishing is a signatory to DORA and promotes assessment of research on its own merits rather than by journal impact factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DORA challenges use of the impact factor as the main means of evaluation. To move focus away from impact factor, the publisher offers a variety of journal- and article-based metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Member of the Initiative for Open Citations (I4OC); all references in published articles are made openly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promoting unrestricted availability of scholarly citation data enhances discoverability of published content and benefits those without access to subscription citation databases; supports a global public web of linked scholarly citation data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprints policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The publisher encourages researchers to deposit pre-publication versions of articles in appropriate preprint repositories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posting of preprints is not considered 'prior publication' by the Royal Society journals; this policy is intended to accelerate accessibility and rapid communication of research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship and contributions (CRediT requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: All published articles contain an Authors’ Contributions section which lists the specific contribution of each author using the machine-readable CRediT taxonomy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This records contributor roles in a standardized, machine-readable way to clarify each author's specific contributions to the published article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent peer review (open peer review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain journals operate open peer review via Web of Science Transparent Peer Review by making reviewer reports, the decision letter and associated author responses accessible alongside published articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referee reports are made public under an open access licence (CC-BY). The policy is implemented on Royal Society Open Science, Open Biology, and Proceedings A and B to make the review process as open as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective peer review policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Royal Society Open Science publishes research on the basis of objective peer review: accepts all articles which are scientifically sound and useful to the community without assessing novelty or potential impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objective peer review allows consideration and publication of negative or null results studies; the decision is based on scientific soundness and usefulness rather than novelty/impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered Reports (two-stage review and conditional acceptance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered Reports are articles where methods and proposed analyses are pre-registered and peer-reviewed prior to research (stage 1). High-quality protocols can be provisionally accepted before data collection; once study is complete, stage 2 appraises results and discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If necessary conditions are met and the final study conforms to the initially approved proposal and quality checks, publication is virtually guaranteed. Benefits include reduced publication bias, constructive feedback on design prior to data collection, and acceptance regardless of outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replication studies policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The publisher invites submission of replications of previous studies and has a Replication Policy committing to publishing valid replications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Royal Society Open Science will consider valid replications of studies previously published in its Psychology and Cognitive Neuroscience section or in other journals; the publisher assumes responsibility for the replicability of empirical studies it publishes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open protocols and open code (encouragement/requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open protocols and open code are identified as features of open science that the publisher supports and expects to be shared alongside research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open protocols and code, alongside open data, enable verification and reuse; specifics on licensing and deposition are addressed by the open data policy and supplementary material procedures.
